chapter.title: Extending OpenNLP
chapter.para: OpenNLP extensions allow customization of existing components. Most components define a factory class that can be implemented to control their creation. The implementation class must implement the required interface and have a public no-argument constructor.

section.title: Extension Registry
section.para: Extensions are referenced by class name, for instance the factory entry of a model manifest or the class attribute of a feature generator descriptor. ExtensionLoader resolves such a name first through the ExtensionRegistry, which every OpenNLP module fills with its own factories, serializers, feature generator factories, codecs, trainers and model readers through an ExtensionRegistrar service. A registered extension is created by the registered supplier, without reflection, which also makes it usable in a GraalVM native image (see ).

A custom extension is registered the same way: implement ExtensionRegistrar, list the class in META-INF/services/opennlp.tools.util.ext.ExtensionRegistrar of the jar that ships it, and register each extension under its class:
An application can also call ExtensionRegistry.getDefault().register(...) at startup. A registered class needs no allowlist entry.

section.title: Extension Class Allowlist
section.para: A class name that is not registered is loaded by ExtensionLoader via reflection. Only classes whose fully-qualified name starts with a registered package prefix are permitted on that path. The default prefix is opennlp..
